page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, providing 16 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The instance configuration allocates 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 35 MB of shared L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and instruction set extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES.

The instance does not bundle local disk storage, necessitating remote block storage attachments for persistent file systems, and it includes no hardware GPU acceleration. Networking is backed by a 5 Gbps baseline bandwidth capacity. In synthetic and practical benchmarking, the instance performs solidly within the middle tier across multi-threaded evaluations, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,299.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 15,380.43. Memory throughput scales to 88.67 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 45.93 GB/sec for writes. Redis SET operations achieve 13.44 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 11.29 GB/sec.

A clear performance tradeoff appears in single-threaded throughput. Single-core stress-ng tests (1,311.19) and single-threaded compression tests like gzip (22.76 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (8.81 GB/sec) fall into the lower quartile, whereas parallelized multi-threaded tasks scale adequately across the 16 vCPUs. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile offers standard compute density without the overhead of unneeded memory capacity or attached local storage. This profile matches parallelized computation workloads, continuous integration pipelines, batch text or data processing, and front-end web serving fleets.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.4xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 virtual instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. Configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading) and 32.0 GB of RAM, the instance features a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation. It supports AVX-512 vector extensions, includes no local storage or GPU accelerators, and delivers 5 Gbps of baseline network throughput. Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier multi-threaded compute and memory bandwidth, scoring 15,380.43 in PassMark CPU and 7,299.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests, alongside 13.44 million Redis SET operations per second. Single-core processing shows weaker relative results in compression and synthetic benchmarks. Given its balanced multi-core throughput and moderate memory footprint, the instance fits web application serving, batch processing, build automation, and distributed application tasks.
